messages:
ana: Quick follow-up on session affinity + retries for streaming requests — want to pick an approach before the RFC next week. TL;DR: sticky connections vs resume tokens vs moving session state to a simple session service. Thoughts?

sam: Sticky at the gateway is simplest for resume semantics (same backend keeps KV cache & model state) but it makes the gateway stateful and complicates scaling/HA. if a node dies you lose active sessions.

lee: Agree. An alternative is an explicit resume token: backend writes short checkpoint (seq num + KV pointer) to a central store and returns resume token in trailers. Client reconnects with token, gateway routes to any backend that can load the checkpoint.

maria: Resume token + central store seems good for reliability, but adds round trips and storage op on every checkpoint. cost and latency implications for high-qps streams.

ana: @maria small correction — i think ana meant "every checkpoint" for infrequent keyframes, not token per token. we can choose checkpoint cadence (e.g., every n tokens or important frames). :+1:

lee: Example headers/payload we prototyped:
```
Request: POST /v1/stream
Headers:
  Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
  X-Redwood-Resume-Token: <optional-token>

Trailers (on checkpoint):
  grpc-status: 0
  x-resume-token: <base64(checkpoint-id)>
```

sam: That handshake works. Two major tradeoffs: 1) where to store checkpoint (in-memory on backend, Redis, or disk-backed store) 2) who owns routing logic to find the right backend for token (gateway vs controlplane service).

maria: From ops POV: Redis TTL-based checkpoints (short lived, e.g. 5m) + ephemeral in-memory cache on backends seems fine. If a backend has the checkpoint in RAM we avoid a read, else fallback to Redis.

lee: Also consider idempotency semantics for partial responses. If client retries with same Idempotency-Key but no resume token — should gateway treat it as fresh request or rejection? We need clear API contract.

tim: I'd push for strong explicit contract: "If Idempotency-Key + no resume token => server may process from scratch (dedupe best-effort). If resume token provided => server must resume from token, or return 410/INVALID_TOKEN." Keeps gateway logic simpler.

sam: For the routing piece: prefer gateway to be stateless and call an "edge-session-service" that maps resume-token -> candidate backends (with health info). That allows autoscaler to move traffic w/o gateway complexity.

maria: +1 on edge-session-service. gives us observability surface and throttling. But that becomes a new critical path for low-latency resumes — ensure it is small and highly cached.

lee: Implementation note: checkpoint should be small (seq index + pointer to KV shard). We can store heavy KV in objectstore and fetch on resume. Backend can incrementally fetch missing KV.

deploy-bot: deploy: edge-session-service v0.2 rolled to staging at 2026-03-18T11:12Z — includes token->backend mapping endpoint.

ana: Ops question: what about sticky sessions for very short streams (e.g., < 5s)? Could we keep short-lived sticky routing to reduce complexity and only use resume tokens for longer streams?

sam: Adaptive strategy makes sense: default sticky for <=X seconds or <=N tokens. For longer sessions require resume token semantics. avoids extra store ops for bursty short requests.

maria: Need to be careful with load balancing — short sticky windows still require consistent hashing or consistent-session assignment to avoid hotspots.

lee: Also need to document failure modes: (a) backend crash -> session lost unless checkpoint persisted, (b) network partition -> client reconnect may hit different region -> token must be region-aware or globally accessible.

ana: Proposal for RFC:
- Gateway remains stateless for routing decisions.
- Introduce edge-session-service (lightweight) to resolve resume-token -> backend candidates.
- Checkpoint policy: conservative default (checkpoint every 256 tokens or on explicit checkpoint request).
- Storage: Redis TTL + objectstore for large KV. Backends keep small cache.
- API contract: Idempotency-Key semantics + resume token behavior documented.
- Adaptive sticky fallback for very short streams to avoid overhead.

tim: Sounds good. For rollout plan: implement session-service + resume-token prototype behind feature flag, test failover scenarios and SLOs, then update SDKs with header semantics.

ana: I'll draft the RFC with decision matrix and a short perf model (cost of Redis ops vs extra latency) — pinging @lee @sam @maria for review tomorrow.

lee: Will review. Also add observability at token lifecycle (issued, used, expired) and per-token size metrics.

maria: Add oncall playbook entry for token-store outage (how to fall back to sticky routing or reject new long-lived streams).

sam: One more: encryption of resume tokens (signed, short-lived) to avoid leaking internal pointers.

ana: Good catch. Resume token should be opaque and signed.

ana: OK closing this thread — RFC draft coming in ~6h. Thanks everyone :rocket:
